title: Bishop v. Eaton — notice from afar
shortTitle: Bishop v. Eaton — notice from afar
summary: The note requires notice when the offeror would not promptly learn of the offeree’s completed act.
notes:
Casebook discussion of a shorter authority.

Eaton, in Nova Scotia, promised to stand behind help to his brother in Illinois. Bishop provided a guarantee, ultimately paid, and sought recovery. The court concluded both that notice was called for in the circumstances and that it had been given. Contrast Carlill’s inferred waiver of advance notice.

sources.label: Farnsworth et al., Contracts: Cases and Materials, 10th ed. (2023), pp. 229. Open assigned page 229.
